segments.t: When we had departed from them
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: and had set sail,
we came with a straight course to Cos,
segments.note: 「with a straight course」は εὐθυδρομήσαντες の表現

segments.t: and the next day to Rhodes,
and from there to Patara.
Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia,
we went aboard and set sail.
When we had come in sight of Cyprus,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: leaving it on the left hand,
we sailed to Syria
and landed at Tyre,
for the ship was there to unload her cargo.
Having found disciples,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we stayed there seven days.
These said to Paul through the Spirit
that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
segments.note: 「that he should」は μὴ＋不定詞の表現

segments.t: When those days were over,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we departed and went on our journey.
They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city.
Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
After saying goodbye to each other,
segments.note: 「saying goodbye」は ἀπησπασάμεθα の表現

segments.t: we went on board the ship,
and they returned home again.
segments.note: 「home」は τὰ ἴδια（自分の家）の表現

segments.t: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we arrived at Ptolemais.
We greeted the brothers
and stayed with them one day.
On the next day,
we who were Paul’s companions departed
segments.note: 「who were Paul’s companions」はビザンティン本文の οἱ περὶ τὸν Παῦλον の訳。ギリシャ語本文にこの句はない

segments.t: and came to Caesarea.
We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist,
who was one of the seven,
and stayed with him.
Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
segments.note: 「had」は ἦσαν＋与格（彼のものとしてあった）の表現

segments.t: As we stayed there some days,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし。「we」は属格絶対構文の含意

segments.t: a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
Coming to us
and taking Paul’s belt,
he bound his own feet and hands,
and said,
“The Holy Spirit says:
‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind
the man who owns this belt,
and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
When we heard these things,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: both we and the people of that place
segments.note: 「people of that place」は ἐντόπιοι 一語の表現

segments.t: begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
Then Paul answered,
“What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart?
For I am ready
segments.note: 「am ready」は ἑτοίμως ἔχω の慣用表現

segments.t: not only to be bound,
but also to die at Jerusalem
for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
When he would not be persuaded,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we ceased, saying,
“The Lord’s will be done.”
After these days
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: we took up our baggage
segments.note: 「took up our baggage」は ἐπισκευασάμενοι の表現

segments.t: and went up to Jerusalem.
Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: bringing one Mnason
of Cyprus,
an early disciple,
with whom we would stay.
When we had come to Jerusalem,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the brothers received us gladly.
The day following,
Paul went in with us to James;
and all the elders were present.
When he had greeted them,
he reported one by one
the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.
They, when they heard it, glorified God.
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: They said to him,
“You see, brother,
how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed,
and they are all zealous for the law.
They have been informed about you,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: that you teach
all the Jews who are among the Gentiles
to forsake Moses,
segments.note: 「to forsake Moses」は ἀποστασίαν ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως の表現

segments.t: telling them not to circumcise their children
and not to walk after the customs.
What then?
The assembly must certainly meet,
segments.note: 「The assembly must … meet」はビザンティン本文の補い（συνελεύσεται πλῆθος）。「certainly」は πάντως の訳で本来は次句の ἀκούσονται にかかる

segments.t: for they will hear that you have come.
Therefore do what we tell you.
We have four men who have taken a vow.
Take them and purify yourself with them,
and pay their expenses for them,
that they may shave their heads.
Then all will know
that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you,
segments.note: 「no truth」は οὐδέν ἐστιν（何でもない）の意訳

segments.t: but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
But concerning the Gentiles who believe,
we have written our decision
segments.note: 「written」は ἀπεστείλαμεν（手紙を送った）の訳

segments.t: that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from
segments.note: WEB は「そのようなことは守らなくてよい、ただし…」と展開訳する。ギリシャ語本文は φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτούς のみ

segments.t: food offered to idols,
from blood,
from strangled things,
and from sexual immorality.”
Then Paul took the men,
and the next day
purified himself
and went with them into the temple,
declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification,
until the offering was offered for every one of them.
When the seven days were almost completed,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: the Jews from Asia,
when they saw him in the temple,
stirred up all the multitude
and laid hands on him,
crying out,
“Men of Israel, help!
This is the man
who teaches all men everywhere
against the people, and the law, and this place.
Moreover, he also brought Greeks
into the temple
and has defiled this holy place!”
For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian
with him in the city,
and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
All the city was moved
and the people ran together.
They seized Paul
and dragged him out of the temple.
Immediately the doors were shut.
As they were trying to kill him,
news came up
to the commanding officer of the regiment
that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
segments.note: 「was in an uproar」は συγχύννεται の表現

segments.t: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions
and ran down to them.
They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers,
stopped beating Paul.
Then the commanding officer came near,
arrested him,
commanded him to be bound with two chains,
and inquired who he was and what he had done.
Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd.
When he couldn’t find out the truth
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: because of the noise,
he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
When he came to the stairs,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: he was carried by the soldiers
because of the violence of the crowd;
for the multitude of the people followed after,
crying out, “Away with him!”
As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks,
he asked the commanding officer,
“May I speak to you?”
He said,
“Do you know Greek?
Aren’t you then the Egyptian
who before these days stirred up to sedition
segments.note: 「to sedition」は ἀναστατώσας（騒乱を起こした）に含まれる

segments.t: and led out into the wilderness
the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
But Paul said,
“I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia,
segments.note: μὲν は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: a citizen of no insignificant city.
I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
When he had given him permission,
segments.note: δὲ は英語に現れないので対応なし

segments.t: Paul, standing on the stairs,
beckoned with his hand to the people.
When there was a great silence,
he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
